claims.claim: Aurora's Q2 2026 disclosure shows commercial scaling has begun: nearly 440,000 driverless miles through June, 100% on-time performance, zero Aurora Driver-attributed collisions, and capacity fully allocated to a 200-truck year-end target.
Roush had begun manufacturing the second-generation fleet and Aurora expected a 1,000-truck annual production run-rate in October, creating a near-term scale checkpoint.

risks.risk: Q2 revenue was only $2M while operating loss was $266M and operating cash use about $225M; scaling remains capital intensive.

unknowns.unknown: The October manufacturing run-rate and year-end 200-truck target have not yet been independently verified as achieved.

claims.claim: Aurora reaffirmed 2026 revenue of $14M-$16M, expected more than half in Q4, and linked the 200-truck exit target to an approximately $80M TaaS revenue run-rate.
Execution should be judged against the October 1,000-truck manufacturing run-rate, year-end 200 driverless trucks, and conversion toward DaaS in 2027 rather than headline partnerships alone.

risks.risk: Back-end-loaded revenue and high cash use make missed deployment milestones materially important.

unknowns.unknown: Unit economics and durable DaaS gross margins at scaled commercial utilization remain unproven in this source.
